## Summary
Replicas are feasible because read methods are already marked read-only, but read-after-write breaks under replication lag. Fix the `$lastn` N+1 first; it dominates database load today.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |

| ARC-001 | info | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/service/PatientService.java:23 | Read methods are `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` | Route on the read-only flag with an `AbstractRoutingDataSource` behind a `LazyConnectionDataSourceProxy`. |
| ARC-002 | medium | correctness | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/api/PatientController.java:47 | POST returns 201 + Location; a GET right after can hit a replica with replication lag and return 404 | Send reads that follow a write in the same client flow to the primary, or document the lag window. |
| ARC-003 | medium | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/service/ObservationService.java:69 | The known $lastn N+1 (`TEACHING-DEFECT(perf-n+1)`, sample-app/docs/KNOWN_DEFECTS.md) issues 2 queries per subject | Measure with it in mind before adding replicas; fixing it is a separate, explicitly scoped ticket. |

## Decisions
- Defer replicas until the N+1 fix and a load test show the primary is the bottleneck.
